auth_description: Use your operator account to manage the proxy control plane.
canvas_list_description: Every proxy topology this control plane manages.
canvas_list_empty_description: Create a canvas to start describing a proxy topology.
canvas_create_description: Name the topology this canvas will describe.
canvas_edit_description: Both the name and the description are replaced.
canvas_delete_warning: Deleting {name} also deletes every server, node, port and edge on it. Workers keep serving their last configuration until they are reconfigured. This cannot be undone.
editor_empty_description: Add a server or a node to start describing the topology.
editor_override_none: Leave empty to use the derived value.
editor_member_count_hint: Between 2 and 256. Disconnect a member before removing it.
editor_pod_orphan: {count} pods point at an IP this canvas does not own
editor_force_description: The control plane refused this deletion. Forcing it skips validation and can leave the canvas invalid.
editor_narrow_description: This canvas is not supported on mobile devices with a narrow screen. Open it on a wider display.
editor_subcanvas_create_description: Creates a canvas and embeds it here as one node. Open it to describe what is inside.
editor_subcanvas_import_description: Embeds an existing canvas. Only canvases outside this tree that nothing else imports can be embedded.
editor_subcanvas_name_hint: Used for both the new canvas and the node that embeds it.
editor_subcanvas_none_importable: No canvas is available to import.
editor_subcanvas_target_fixed: The embedded canvas cannot be changed. Delete this node and import again instead.
editor_subcanvas_ports_hint: One port per export node inside the embedded canvas, named after it.
editor_export_create_description: An export is one boundary port of this canvas: the canvas that embeds it sees a port with this name.
editor_export_direction_hint: Named from inside: an inward export feeds this canvas, an outward one feeds the parent.
editor_export_name_hint: The parent labels the mirrored port with this name.
editor_export_reshape_warning: Changing the kind or direction drops the edge attached to this port in the parent canvas.
health_description: How the workers serving this canvas are doing.
health_placeholder_description: Worker health for this canvas will appear here.
settings_description: The name and description of this canvas, and its removal.
settings_danger_description: Removes the canvas with every server, node, port and edge on it.
help_description: How to describe a proxy topology on the canvas.
help_usage_description: A canvas is a graph: servers and nodes joined by edges between their ports.
help_step_add_body: Use the buttons in the top-left corner. Each one drops a new item in the middle of the view.
help_step_edit_body: Click a node to open its panel on the right. Drag the divider to resize it; close it with the X.
help_step_connect_body: Drag from an output port to an input port. Only compatible ports accept the connection.
help_step_arrange_body: Drag nodes to move them; their position is saved when you drop them. Drag the empty background to pan and scroll to zoom.
help_step_problems_body: Validation problems are listed in the bottom-left corner. Click one to jump to the node it concerns, opening its canvas first when the node lives in a subcanvas.
help_step_subcanvas_body: A subcanvas is a whole canvas drawn as one node. Double-click it to go inside; add export nodes there and the parent gains a matching port for each of them.
help_step_delete_body: Select nodes or edges and press Delete. The control plane refuses deletions that would break the topology; administrators can force them.
help_keys_description: Shortcuts work while the canvas has focus, not while typing in the panel.
help_key_delete: Delete the selected nodes and edges
help_key_multi_select: Add a node or edge to the selection
help_key_focus: Move focus to the next node
help_key_nudge: Nudge the selected nodes by 5 pixels
help_key_nudge_fast: Nudge the selected nodes by 20 pixels
help_key_pan: Pan the view, even over nodes
